scope: Synthetic static reference likelihood; no native data, model, optimizer, novelty or scientific-admission evidence.

equations.cost: O(Q*K) scalar relation scores; no superpoint NxN attention

checks: Nine target-supervised partials agree with finite differences.
No anchor labels are needed for a nonzero anchor-logit gradient.
Without interaction, anchor probabilities cancel out of target likelihood.
Additively separable relation scores also give zero anchor gradient.
Joint anchor permutation preserves the target likelihood.
Anchor unary/relation gauge prevents unique internal parameter identification.
A nonseparable relation change can change supervised target probability.
conclusion: Lack of direct auxiliary-anchor labels is not a universal no-learning theorem. Nonzero gradient is not correct-anchor identification or causal efficacy. Generic target-supervised latent relations are prior art and not a proposed new variant.
